title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: The changes only add permission checks and use Django ORM serializers; no raw SQL or string‑concatenated queries are introduced.

Permission is checked before retrieving the stream object, but the code does not verify that the fetched stream actually belongs to the provider associated with the request. This could allow an IDOR where a user with the required permission on one provider accesses or modifies a stream belonging to another provider by supplying its ID.

evidence.content:
if not request.user.has_perm("authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream", self.provider):
    raise PermissionDenied(...)
stream = self.get_object()
serializer = StreamSerializer(stream, data=request.data, partial=True)

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure that `self.get_object()` (or an explicit check) validates that the retrieved Stream instance is associated with `self.provider`. For example, filter by both `pk` and `provider` or raise PermissionDenied if `stream.provider != self.provider`.
